We're researching JIRA ticket SFCC-237 for the Zimmermann Salesforce PWA Kit project (repo root: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa). SFCC-237 is a "Spike" whose deliverable is a TSD (technical spec doc) comparing MRT (Managed Runtime) *application* topology options: (A) a single MRT app hosting all integrations (today's default), (B) a dedicated MRT app per integration/domain, or a middle option of one modular app. It's scored on deploy/rollback, failure isolation (event-loop/memory/process — not just network sockets), secrets/security blast radius, performance/LCP, cost, and ownership.

A prior spike-audit session (11 days ago) already established an "as-is baseline" and found two discrepancies. We need you to VERIFY whether these are still true today (things may have changed — there have been several recent commits/PRs about tagging, CI/CD, and a new storefront) and fill in some additional gaps. Do NOT just trust the prior findings — re-check each one against the current repo state and report what you actually find, flagging anything that has changed.

Please investigate and report back on ALL of the following, citing exact file paths and line numbers / exact code or config snippets as evidence for each claim:

1. **`mobify.config.js` / MRT push-target resolution — how does it actually work in this PWA Kit version?**
   - Confirm whether `mobify.config.js` exists anywhere in the repo (it was reported absent 11 days ago despite being referenced in docs).
   - Check `package.json` (root) for a top-level `"mobify"` key/object — in some PWA Kit versions the MRT project config (project slug, per-target settings) lives there instead of a separate `mobify.config.js` file. Report its exact contents if present.
   - Check `package.json` `scripts` for anything with `push`, `pwa-kit-dev push`, `activate`, or `-t <target>` — report the exact script lines.
   - Grep `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/` (and `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/` if relevant) for how it resolves a push target: search for the strings `mobify.config`, `"mobify"`, and `config.mobify` in that package's source/dist. Report what you find — does this PWA Kit version actually support/expect a `mobify.config.js` file at all, or has it been superseded by the `package.json` "mobify" key? This directly resolves whether the "missing mobify.config.js" is a real gap or a stale doc reference to a mechanism this version doesn't even use.
   - Cross check package.json's declared version of `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev` / `@salesforce/retail-react-app`.

2. **Environment / config topology as actually implemented in code:**
   - Full listing of `config/` directory contents (`ls -la`).
   - For `config/default.js` and `config/sites.js`: report the `ssrParameters.proxyConfigs` entries (proxy origins configured) — confirm whether it's still only SCAPI + OCAPI, or whether mulesoft/google/booxi/other proxy entries have been added since.
   - List which per-tier config files exist (e.g. `dev.js`, `sit.js`, `test.js`, `uat.js`, `staging.js`, `production.js`) — report exactly which tier names have a corresponding file and which don't.
   - List every file under `.github/workflows/` matching `deploy-*.yml` and, for each, report: which GitHub Environment it targets (`environment:` key), and the exact MRT push command / target it uses (grep for `pwa-kit-dev push`, `-t `, `npm run push`).

3. **Blast-radius / undici connection pool wiring — is it still inert?**
   - Read `overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts` in full — report what pools it defines.
   - Grep the whole `overrides/` tree for `connectionPools`, `dispatcher`, and each pool name it exports (e.g. `sfcc-scapi`, `mulesoft`, etc.) to see whether anything actually imports/uses them now (previously: imported nowhere, `dispatcher` attached to no real `fetch()`).
   - Read `overrides/app/ssr.js` and the other files under `overrides/app/ssr/` (`slasTokens.ts`, `paymentMetadata.ts`, `marketingCloud.ts`, and any others present) — for each `fetch()` call, report whether it passes a `dispatcher` option or uses the global dispatcher.
   - Read `overrides/app/request-processor.js` — report whether it's still the unmodified Salesforce example stub or has real Zimmermann logic now.
   - Read `worker/main.js` — report its current content/purpose.

4. **`.docs/integration/` directory** — list all files (`ls`), confirm the count (previously reported as ~18 numbered docs), and report any file that looks newly added in the last ~2 weeks (check `git log --oneline -- .docs/integration/` since 2026-07-30).

5. **CODEOWNERS** (`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/CODEOWNERS`) — report the exact lines/patterns covering `config/`, `worker/`, `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `overrides/app/ssr/`, `mobify.config.js` if present, and `.github/workflows/`.

6. **`.docs/prd/regional.md`** — skim for any content about MRT app topology, per-site routing to different apps/processes, or anything relevant to "how many MRT apps do we run." Report relevant excerpts only if they exist; otherwise say it's silent on this.

7. **`.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`** — skim for any mention of MRT topology, multiple apps, or per-app deploy targets. Report relevant excerpts only if they exist; otherwise say it's silent on this.

8. **Recent git history for context** — run `git log --oneline --since=2026-07-30 -- worker/main.js overrides/app/ssr.js overrides/app/ssr/ mobify.config.js config/ .github/workflows/ package.json CODEOWNERS` and report the commits found (there may be none — that's a valid finding).

9. **Broad grep sweep** — grep the whole repo (excluding `node_modules/`, `.git/`) case-insensitively for `per-integration`, `per-app`, `MRT app`, `MRT application`, `multiple MRT`, and `topology` — report every hit with file:line, in case there's a relevant reference we haven't already found in `.docs/architecture.md` or `.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md` (we've already read those two files ourselves, no need to re-read them, just don't miss anything if grep hits them — just note "already known" for those two files).

Report your findings as a structured list matching the 9 items above, each with file:line citations and exact quoted evidence. Where something is absent, explicitly say "not found" / "does not exist" rather than omitting it. This is a fact-finding pass to support writing a technical spec doc — precision and explicit sourcing matter more than brevity.

The key insight here is that `getConfig` from the Salesforce PWA Kit runtime v3.18.0 leverages `cosmiconfig` to search for configuration files in a specific order—checking `config/{DEPLOY_TARGET}.ext`, `config/local.ext`, and `config/default.ext` before falling back to the `mobify` property in `package.json`.

This means there's no dedicated `mobify.config.js` file at the root level; instead, the naming convention follows the `config/` directory structure. While `package.json`'s `mobify` key is technically a valid fallback location, it has the lowest priority and would be overridden by `config/default.js` (which always exists in PWA Kit projects), making it essentially irrelevant for SSR config resolution. 60	## 2. Entry Routing & Mismatch Detection (REG-009, REG-013 – REG-035)
61	
62	- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
63	- **AU is gated** to AU and NZ/Pacific Island IPs only (REG-009). AU is the `x-default` hreflang and must remain crawlable, so it is never blocked at the network level. A non-AU/non-Oceania human visitor landing on AU is redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; if no storefront matches their region, fall back to HK. Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect — match by User-Agent against a comprehensive allowlist (Googlebot incl. Image/News, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, AppleBot, YandexBot, Baiduspider, Slackbot, Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp, Discordbot). Fail open: if UA looks botty but isn't matched, skip the redirect rather than apply it — false-positive cost is zero, missing a real crawler hurts SEO.
64	- All other storefronts use **mismatch detection** (REG-014): a country slide-out is shown on the first visit if the user's IP country does not match the storefront's shipping region (REG-015). Two CTAs: redirect to the appropriate storefront, or open the country selector (REG-016). A warning is shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-017). Not shown if country matches (REG-018). Shown on first visit only — does not reappear after selection or dismissal (REG-019).
65	- **Country + language selector** available on all storefronts except AU (REG-020, REG-025). Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display and search field (REG-021). Warning shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-022). Country and language combined in the same selector; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES, all other storefronts English only (REG-023). Selected EU locale reflected in URL (REG-024).
66	- AU is gated and does **not** allow inbound cross-navigation from other sites (REG-025).
67	- **China** selected from any country selector routes to HK (REG-026).
68	- **Australia** selected from another storefront's country selector (i.e. clients outside Oceania) routes to HK (REG-027).
69	- Global-e checkout locks the shipping country — determined by country selector pre-checkout, cannot be changed inside Global-e (REG-028).

71	### EU language mismatch (REG-029 – REG-035)
72	
73	When a user's GEO-IP country doesn't match the URL language on the EU domestic storefront, show a language mismatch modal in the current URL language (REG-029, REG-031). Two CTAs: continue in current language, or switch (REG-032). Country-to-language mapping (REG-030):
74	
75	- France / Monaco → French (`/fr-eu/`)
76	- Italy / San Marino → Italian (`/it-eu/`)
77	- Spain → Spanish (`/es-eu/`)
78	
79	Modal does not show when detected country matches the current URL language (REG-033), and is not shown for countries with no dedicated EU locale — they default to `/en-eu/` (REG-034). Logic applies regardless of entry point (Instagram, Google Shopping, direct URL, organic search) (REG-035).

83	## 3. Checkout Ownership
84	
85	- **SFCC** owns domestic checkout for AU (REG-003), UK (REG-004), US domestic (REG-005), EU domestic (REG-006 dom).
86	- **Global-e** owns checkout for HK (REG-007), ME (REG-008), US international (REG-005 — now a separate SFCC site), EU international (REG-006 intl) — and for any domestic storefront when the customer's selected shipping destination is outside the domestic market.
87	- **AU serves Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands) domestically** via SFCC — not via Global-e. Avalara calculates duties/tax for NZ and New Caledonia specifically (REG-003); other Oceania destinations are DDU.
88	- Branch checkout ownership at PDP/cart, not only at the checkout page.
89	- **Global-e pricing via SFCC price books (REG-041, Confirmed 05-05):** SFCC holds all price books including for Global-e markets. AP21 feeds base RRP pricebooks per currency (AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) and fixed pricelists per Global-e market to SFCC via MuleSoft. A nightly job generates Global-e-derived pricebooks using FX rates and coefficients from Global-e. Global-e handles shipping charges, duties, and taxes at checkout. SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency to Global-e. SFCC does **not** independently calculate shipping, duties, or tax for Global-e paths. (REG-040 was retired 05-05 — superseded by REG-041.)

97	- Single currency per domestic storefront: AUD, USD, GBP, EUR (REG-039). No multi-currency toggle. (Open: Zimmermann would like multi-currency on AU domestic to offer NZD — not yet agreed.)

The EU domestic site supports one RRP but must support multiple EU zone VAT requirements in the order payload. US domestic: prices excl. tax; Avalara calculates sales tax at checkout (REG-038). NZ and New Caledonia on AU: Avalara (REG-037).
99	- Sale pricing: was/now format. If price changes again after sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042).

128	| Storefront                   | Default                                          |

141	
142	- Marketing opt-in checkbox displayed at two points: guest checkout entry page and account registration page. Unchecked by default on all storefronts **except US (pre-checked)** (REG-057).
143	- Opt-in state sync: FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys. Passed to Omneo on order placement for guests, on account registration for registered customers (REG-058).

151	
152	- Customer support chat widget shown on relevant pages per Inside Chat's own display rules.

158

The actual mechanism, traced end-to-end:

- `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/bin/pwa-kit-dev.js:395`: `const mobify = getConfig({buildDirectory}) || {}` — the push command's config comes from `getConfig()`, imported at line 16 from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-config`.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-config.server.js:59-75` — `getConfig()` uses `cosmiconfig` with `packageProp: 'mobify'` and this exact `searchPlaces` order: `config/{DEPLOY_TARGET}.{js,yml,yaml,json}` → `config/local.{ext}` (local dev only) → `config/default.{ext}` → `package.json`. **A root `mobify.config.js` filename is never in this search list in this version.**
